title: For a non-replicate EMA study, 4.1.8 rounds the CI bounds and ICH M13A 2.2.4 does not
raised_by: PR #88, the audit that was opened to add 4.1.8 rounding to EMA standard ABE and found it would be wrong

ema_2010_guideline_4_1_8.rule: To be inside the acceptance interval the lower bound should be >= 80.00% when rounded to two decimal places and the upper bound should be <= 125.00% when rounded to two decimal places.
ema_2010_guideline_4_1_8.source: EMA, Guideline on the Investigation of Bioequivalence, CPMP/EWP/QWP/1401/98 Rev. 1, section 4.1.8
ema_2010_guideline_4_1_8.scope: the BE criteria paragraph for single-dose studies

ich_m13a_2_2_4.rule: The 90% confidence interval for the geometric mean ratio of these PK parameters used to establish BE should lie within a range of 80.00 - 125.00%.
ich_m13a_2_2_4.source: ICH M13A, EMA Step 5 (EMA/CHMP/ICH/953493/2022), section 2.2.4, within 2.2 'Data Analysis for Non-Replicate Study Design'

ema_m13a_qa.source: ICH M13A Questions and Answers, EMA/CHMP/ICH/325575/2024, 17 pages
ema_m13a_qa.result: no occurrence of any term; the only match for 'round' is the word 'around' in the preface

ema_531548_2024.source: EMA/531548/2024, Considerations regarding the implementation of ICH M13A, adopted by CHMP 17 February 2025
ema_531548_2024.supersession: ICH M13A came into effect on 25 January 2025, 'formally superseding applicable parts of' the 2010 guideline
ema_531548_2024.scope_of_m13a: 'ICH M13A, however, only relates to BE study considerations and data analysis for a non-replicate study design'; its data-analysis considerations include 'BE criteria'
ema_531548_2024.transition: BE studies completed and included in a regulatory submission before 25 January 2025 keep the requirements of the EMA guideline; submissions after that date should follow ICH M13A
ema_531548_2024.replicate_designs: BE studies with highly variable drugs (replicate design) and drugs with narrow therapeutic index are named as topics where both documents are read in conjunction

what_be_stats_does.non_replicate_routes: One comparison, `spec.ci_within_limits`: the CI lies within the limits, inclusive at both ends, compared as computed. Called by `AcceptanceInterval.contains` (the standard route, EMA and FDA alike) and by `ema_nti._interval_contained` (EMA 4.1.9).
what_be_stats_does.replicate_ema_hvd: Unchanged. `ema_hvd._interval_contained` rounds against 80.00-125.00% under 4.1.8, because M13A does not cover replicate designs and EMA/531548/2024 keeps the 2010 guideline for them.
what_be_stats_does.submission_date: Not an input. The engine cannot tell a pre-2025 study from a later one.

what_changed_in_this_pr: EMA 4.1.9 (PR #87) rounded both bounds on 4.1.8's authority, while the standard route compared unrounded and cited M13A 2.2.4. A crossover against 80.00-125.00% therefore got two different comparisons from one regulator depending on the route. EMA 4.1.9 now uses the standard route's comparison. No standard-route or FDA result moves.
why_unrounded: For a non-replicate study submitted after 25 January 2025, M13A governs the BE criteria and its text does not round. For a study submitted before, 4.1.8 applies and rounds; the unrounded comparison is then the stricter reading - any interval that passes unrounded also passes rounded, and never the reverse - so it can refuse a study 4.1.8 would pass by up to 0.005 on a bound, and cannot pass one 4.1.8 would refuse.
what_would_close_it: An EMA statement on whether the two-decimal practice of 4.1.8 continues under M13A, or a typed submission-regime input so a pre-2025 study is compared under 4.1.8.
action_required: None in be-stats until one of those exists.
